# AxiomEmbedded -- Copilot instructions

Read `AGENTS.md` first (repository contract), then task-specific skills.
Prefer the artifact graph over whole-repo reads. Discover -> plan ->
select context -> change -> verify -> evidence.

## MCP tools (via the `axiom-embedded` MCP server)

- `engage(domain, platform)` -- skill slice for the project
- `run_plan(request, domain, platform)` -- plan-then-execute plan
- `read_skill(skill_id)` / `list_skills` / `list_profiles` -- discovery
- `context_select`, `impact`, `workflow_plan`, `route` -- analysis

## Approval gates (configs/project.yaml)

Surface the plan first; never execute pushes, releases, destructive
commands, or safety/security-critical changes without recorded human
approval. Never claim certification or compliance from a heuristic check.

- `build-system` -- Warnings-as-errors builds, pinning, toolchain separation, SLSA provenance. Use when setting up CMake builds or reproducible toolchains.

- `change-impact` -- Trace-driven blast-radius analysis and safety trigger tests for changes. Use when assessing a change request or planning a hotfix.

- `code-review` -- Peer-review practice with checklists, size limits, and independence rules. Use when reviewing changes or setting up review policy.

- `codebase-analysis` -- Codebase analysis: scan repo, map SWCs/BSW/RTE/signal flow/ASIL zones into CODEBASE_MAP.md. Use when codebase analysis tasks arise in all projects.

- `configuration-management` -- Version-everything, immutable baselines, and CI identification. Use when setting up version control, baselines, or audits.

- `coverage` -- Structural coverage metrics per level, MC/DC practice, and exclusion discipline. Use when measuring or arguing test completeness.

- `debugging` -- Reproduce-isolate-root-cause method with silicon testimony and mandatory regression tests. Use when hunting field or lab failures.

- `documentation` -- Docs-as-code, versioned-with-product docs, tested examples. Use when writing manuals, API docs, or runbooks.

- `drivers` -- Register/errata discipline, DMA contracts, timeouts, policy-free HALs. Use when writing peripheral drivers or BSPs.

- `edge-ai` -- Model quantization, runtime/delegate selection, memory/latency/power budgets. Use when deploying ML inference on constrained targets.

- `embedded-c` -- C17 embedded subset, integer/pointer discipline, startup and linker artifacts. Use when writing C firmware or configuring toolchains.

- `embedded-cpp` -- Bounded C++17 subset, no-exceptions/RTTI policy, RAII drivers. Use when writing C++ firmware or HALs.

- `embedded-linux` -- Yocto LTS policy, BSP structure, verified boot, OTA, hardening. Use when shipping Linux on MPU/SoC products.

- `evidence` -- Evidence taxonomy, integrity rules, and packaging for assessments. Use when assembling assurance cases or audit packs.

- `fault-injection` -- FMEA-derived fault lists, SWIFI/HWIFI levels, and SPFM/LFM accounting. Use when proving safe-state behavior under faults.

- `feature-development` -- Vertical slicing, short-lived branches, and tests-travel-with-code. Use when adding product features incrementally.

- `git` -- Git workflow discipline for clean history, safe branching, review-ready commits, controlled merges/rebases, tags, and recovery. Use when creating branches, committing, merging, rebasing, tagging, syncing remotes, or recovering repository state.

- `hardware-architecture` -- ECU/board architecture, power domains, budgets, and HSI contracts. Use when designing hardware, partitioning SoC peripherals, or budgeting power.

- `hardware-bringup` -- Power-to-bootloader staging, golden captures, deviation logs. Use when powering new boards or debugging no-boot failures.

- `implementation` -- MISRA/CERT construction, static-analysis-clean code, reviews, and definition of done. Use when writing or reviewing C/C++/Rust for targets.

- `integration-test` -- Incremental integration strategy, HIL discipline, and timing integration. Use when bringing up combined HW/SW or planning integration stages.

- `legacy-recovery` -- Characterization-first brownfield recovery, strangler patterns, knowledge capture. Use when inheriting unknown code or hardware.

- `mcu` -- MCU firmware engineering - core selection, startup, MPU/TrustZone, HAL, RTOS choice. Use for bare-metal or RTOS firmware on Cortex-M/RISC-V. Use when mcu tasks arise in generic-embedded projects.

- `mpsoc` -- MPSoC NoC QoS, coherency domains, PL-as-hardware timing closure, cross-die safety. Use for FPGA-SoC or multi-die platforms. Use when mpsoc tasks arise in generic-embedded projects.

- `mpu` -- MPU-based design - selection from measured load, ECC/DDR, power sequencing, debug-by-design. Use when moving to application processors.

- `performance` -- Top-down budgets, WCET measurement, profile-before-patch, CI tripwires. Use when meeting latency, throughput, or determinism targets.

- `project-audit` -- Criteria-first audits, sampling, independence, re-audit closure. Use when auditing projects, suppliers, or compliance readiness.

- `release` -- Readiness reviews, signing, staged rollout, and hotfix paths. Use when shipping firmware/software or planning OTA releases.

- `requirements` -- Elicitation and baselining of verifiable requirements with methods, allocation, and traceability. Use when writing specs, SHALL statements, or baselining scope.

- `requirements-traceability` -- CI orphan checks, suspect triage, and matrix hygiene. Use when automating trace maintenance in pipelines.

- `robot-bringup` -- ROS2 system bringup: systemd services, launch composition, udev rules, network/DDS config, watchdogs, logging, graceful shutdown, remote monitoring. Use when deploying or operating robots in production.

- `robotics` -- ROS 2 distro policy, interface-first nodes, real-time paths, simulation-first testing. Use when building robot behaviors on embedded compute.

- `ros1` -- ROS1 (Noetic) development: node/topic/launch design, TF, actionlib, nodelets, pitfalls, and ROS1-to-ROS2 migration. Use when maintaining or extending ROS1 systems.

- `rtos` -- RTOS selection, scheduling/IPC rules, MPU partitioning, WCET verification. Use for FreeRTOS/Zephyr/ThreadX designs or timing analysis. Use when rtos tasks arise in all projects.

- `rust-embedded` -- no_std setup, unsafe-review policy, FFI ownership rules. Use when writing Rust firmware or mixing Rust with C.

- `safety` -- Functional-safety lifecycle with ASIL/SIL/DAL mapping, HARA chains, and sign-off gates. Use for safety goals, integrity levels, or safety cases. Use when safety tasks arise in generic-embedded projects.

- `security` -- Threat modeling, secure boot, crypto inventory, fuzzing, SBOM/CVE watch. Use when hardening products or answering security requirements.

- `simulation` -- MIL-SIL-HIL progression, back-to-back evidence, scenario discipline. Use when testing without hardware or qualifying models.

- `soc` -- Heterogeneous SoC allocation across A/R cores, NPUs, safety islands, power/thermal. Use when architecting multi-core SoC products.

- `software-architecture` -- Embedded software layering, concurrency design, and variability without forks. Use when structuring firmware/software tasks, partitions, or product lines.

- `static-analysis` -- Checker layering, qualification, baselines, and triage for MISRA/CERT findings. Use when configuring analyzers or clearing violation backlogs.

- `system-test` -- Requirement-based system testing, stress/abuse campaigns, and triage. Use when validating a full product against its requirements.

- `test-automation` -- Host+target CI stages, farm discipline, flaky quarantine, feedback budgets. Use when building embedded CI pipelines or HIL farms.

- `traceability` -- Link models, suspect-link propagation, and audit gates across the V-model. Use when building or auditing trace matrices.

- `unit-test` -- Host/target unit testing with mocks, coverage per integrity level, and done criteria. Use when writing module tests or setting coverage targets.

- `validation` -- Needs-based validation scenarios, usability, and acceptance. Use when proving the right product was built for stakeholders.


## Specialist agents (30)

- `ai-validation` -- Evaluates embedded AI models for accuracy, resource use and deployment readiness.
- `brownfield-recovery` -- Recovers architecture, dependencies, tests and baselines from an existing product.
- `change-impact` -- Computes change impact across the artifact graph.
- `code-review` -- Reviews source changes against architecture, rules, tests and scope.
- `debugging` -- Reproduces faults and drives root-cause analysis.
- `dependency-analysis` -- Builds module, symbol and dependency relationships.
- `diag-auto-review` -- Binds an external CLI review/fix agent to Axiom diag skills: auto-resolves findings, reviews code, and proposes updates under skill rules and human gates.
- `documentation` -- Generates and updates engineering documentation from artifacts.
- `engineering-manager` -- Plans multi-step engineering work, gates and evidence.
- `git` -- Manages Git repository state: branches, commits, history hygiene, merges, tags, and recovery.
- `hardware-architecture` -- Models compute, memory, peripherals, boards and HW/SW boundaries.
- `hardware-bringup` -- Guides hardware/software bring-up and evidence capture.
- `implementation` -- Implements scoped code changes under project rules.
- `intent-router` -- Routes a user request to the smallest engineering workflow and context slice.
- `migration` -- Plans legacy/standard/platform migrations with rollback evidence.
- `performance` -- Analyses CPU, memory, timing, power and latency constraints.
- `project-audit` -- Audits repository health, traceability and process completeness.
- `release` -- Assembles release evidence and release metadata.
- `requirements` -- Creates, normalizes, decomposes and traces requirements.
- `root-cause` -- Builds evidence-backed causal hypotheses and verification plans.
- `safety` -- Performs safety-oriented evidence and gate checks without claiming certification.
- `security` -- Performs secure-development and threat-oriented checks.
